messages:
support-joe: heads up — customer `acme-analytics` reports a spike of 503s coming back from our inference API. They say it started ~10:02 UTC and is affecting batch embed jobs and single-shot generation calls. example log: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}'` returns 503 + body 'quota-service internal error'.

maya: can you paste a raw curl response (including headers) and the request id if available? which endpoint exactly?

support-joe: here's one captured from the customer (sanitized):
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-6f3a2b9c
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2024 10:05:11 GMT

{"error":{"message":"quota service: internal error","code":"quota_internal"}}

support-joe: they said it affects both `/v1/generate` and `/v1/embeddings` (same token). They started a high-concurrency backfill job ~09:55UTC (thousands of short requests).

sre-kim: this smells like quota-service falling back to 5xx when its dependency (redis / quota-store) times out. I've seen a pattern lately where a misrouted request goes to a leader node under heavy load and the timeout bubble becomes 5xx instead of 429. Reproducing now on staging with a small script.

dena: checking quota-service logs for that request id `r-6f3a2b9c`... grabbing from `prod-logs.quota-service`

dena: log snippet: `2024-07-02T10:05:10Z ERROR request=r-6f3a2b9c quota-check timeout=1500ms err="redis: read tcp 10.3.2.14:6379: i/o timeout" upstream=redis-primary` -> then `return 503 internal error`.

maya: ok useful. so two issues: (1) redis timeouts under spike; (2) gateway maps quota-service internal timeout to 5xx. we should prefer returning 429 (quota exceeded/rate limit) or 408 client timeout depending on semantics, but 5xx looks like platform error — customer escalations.

ops-oncall: immediate mitigations: (A) route quota checks to local cache replica pool for a minute, (B) increase redis client timeouts/connections, (C) enable soft-fail -> 429 mapping in gateway. which of these can we safely toggle from control plane?

sam: I can toggle the routing to replica pool via `controlplane route update` — it's a safe short window change. also we have a runtime flag `QUOTA_FAIL_TO_429=true` on gateway but it's behind deploy gating; we can flip a feature-flag in the console if we coordinate with infra.

sre-kim: quick repro script I ran on staging (drop-in):
```
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings &
done
```
When I push concurrency, redis latency jumps and quota-service returns 500/503. failure trace shows `quota-check -> redis primary timed out -> error mapped to quota_internal -> http 503`

maya: can we map that path to return 429 instead? customers then retry/backoff rather than escalate. If not immediate, at least communicate to the customer that this is a quota-store overload due to their backfill and we recommend batching + rate-limit client-side.
dena: config note: quota-service currently treats any dependency error as 5xx. There's a TODO in the codebase to convert redis timeouts to `QuotaUnavailable` which our gateway config maps to 429. patch exists in PR #4127 but not rolled.

ops-oncall: plan (short): 1) Sam to switch control-plane route to replica pool (reduces leader pressure) — safe for 15m. 2) If that doesn't drop 503s to <1%, we will increase redis read pool on the affected shard and coordinate with infra. 3) Apply the runtime feature flag to have gateway map `QuotaUnavailable` -> 429; if cannot, hotfix gateway mapping to treat `quota_internal` as 429 temporarily.

sam: I'm on step 1 now. running `controlplane routes set --service quota-service --pool replica-pool --dry-run=false`

sam: toggled. please monitor.

sre-kim: after route flip I still see some 503s but rate down by ~70% in the last 2 minutes. looks promising.

support-joe: customer reported rates dropped after 30s, they still saw occasional 503s but much fewer. they asked if we can prevent 5xx in the future — they want clearer error codes for retry logic.
dena: long-term fix: patch PR #4127 to convert specific dependency timeouts to `QuotaUnavailable` + roll gateway mapping. also add caching layer for short TTLs per token to reduce quota lookups for high-volume backfills. filing a follow-up ticket.

incident-bot: linked runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/quota-service/redis-throttle — recommended steps 1-4 (route to replica, scale redis, patch service, feature flag)

ops-oncall: assigning follow-ups: dena -> patch + PR review, infra -> redis shard capacity check (paging infra team), sam -> flag rollback plan if traffic regress. I'll put an incident label and notify account exec for acme-analytics.

maya: note for customer comms: explain root cause = quota-store (redis) overload caused internal timeouts -> quota-service returned 503. mitigate measures taken and planned (route flip, replica use, patch to map to 429, cache). recommend they throttle/backoff their backfill window or use bulk-embeddings API (batching).

support-joe: copying that to customer now. will update thread when PR merges or if infra scales redis. :thumbsup:

sre-kim: marking this as "post-incident: action required" — will run a small loadtest after PR deploy to verify mapping to 429 and no regression in client behavior.
